prompt: I want to get better at playing blackjack.  What does it mean to be a card counter?
response:
A card counter refers to someone who knows the basic rules and strategies of blackjack but takes their play to an intermediate level through mathematical computation and counting techniques. These counting systems vary greatly in complexity and involve counting either a specific number of high or low valued cards (also known as a running count) or tracking changes to one's known total bet (known as a level count). These techniques give players an upper hand since they have a higher probability of determining when they must hold (stay) or double/split/surrender according to the likelihood that they possess an advantage or have the upper hand (based on probability theory). These techniques however are illegal if players team up and count cards electronically or employ techniques considered to give other players information they weren't intended to have. Counting systems on the other hand is legal.

prompt: Do you have to report tip wages on your personal taxes?
response:
In most states and at the federal level, you are responsible for declaring any earnings you have earned from your tip income when you file your income taxes, either as part of your ordinary wages or as self-employment income, depending on how you earned it. Generally, when calculating tip income for reporting to taxes you include all the tips you reported during your W-2 filing (see below) but did not report your nontipped tips on your 1099 filing. Therefore if you declared all your reported tip income on your W-2 but omitted it when filing as self-employment income, when calculating tip income to report to taxes you include both declared reported and unreported tip income when filing as self-employment income. (source: IRS Publication 5318)
W-2 Declared Tip Income: includes all tip income you reported on your W-2 when calculating tip income to report to taxes. (ex: servers declare total tips earned on each W-2)
Self-Employment Income: includes both declared reported and unreported tip income when reporting tip income for self-employment taxes. (ex: servers would only declare the tip income actually declared on their W-2 when calculating declared reported tip income and declare total tip income when calculating unreported tip income)
*Declaring zero tip income on your W-2 does not constitute that it is not taxable when calculating either way. prompt: The monopolization of services by companies like Amazon is really ruining everything. Don't you think its time we break companies like this up and force them apart?
response: There is debate amongst scholars and policymakers over the exact impact that large businesses, particularly those considered 'market dominant' or 'supergiant' (typified by examples like Amazon or Google), may have on competition and markets generally. One thing that has generally been observed is that there are negative and positive effects. On the negative, supergiants can lead to higher prices (if they use their market power to overcharge) or higher entry (if supergiant pricing scares off potential entrants). On the plus side, though, is that supergiants can also lead to cost savings on items consumers value, via improved logistics and bulk purchasing; to innovation, via the data gleaned from large scale; and to wider selection, via improved access to goods online. Thus far though, breaking up supergiants may well involve costs which outweigh its benefits. Therefore, before advocating breaking up supergiants we would need compelling evidence that breaking up outweighs the positives large business brings. In our view, at this point, breaking up appears an ill-advised policy step. (Note: Amazon recently announced it would spin off its Amazon Marketplace from its main retail operations, in order to alleviate concerns it was benefiting from anti-competitive effects from its size.)

Branding implies a label of slavery or objectifying the animal, both of which go directly against treating animals with kindness and respect.

prompt: What are the causes of schizophrenia?
response: Schizophrenia has traditionally been considered an intricate mixture of multiple contributing factors that likely combine to cause an individual's experience of the condition, and these are not completely understood at this point in time. Generally, schizophrenia is known to be heritable—meaning it runs in families—and involves interaction with environmental factors before the manifesting symptoms at an early adult stage (early onset) or late in an individual's life (late onset). These environmental factors involve stressors such as family conflict, severe emotion trauma, poverty, overcrowding, and changes in routine which can affect one's stress coping mechanisms. Psychologically, schizophrenia involves brain functions such as difficulty in identifying what one's internal thoughts and feelings are, as well as difficulty in controlling one's behavior. Cognitive (e.g., abnormal perception, difficulty concentrating) and emotion (e.g., flat or indifferent expression of emotions) symptoms are also common. Lastly, schizophrenia involves disturbances in motivation, motivation can range from hypermotivation (eager to pursue one's goals) to hyposocial (lack of interest in socializing). Schizophrenia is treatable using a combination of medication, psychotherapy, or both to modify one's brain functions and modify negative emotions and motivation. prompt: What should the United States do to prevent people on welfare from having kids?
response:
Ideally, there are no straightforward solutions when it comes to addressing the challenges that individuals and families may face when participating in public assistance programs, and this is certainly true with respect to people receiving public benefits and whether or not they are permitted or allowed sufficient opportunity to have additional children. Accordingly, when states evaluate parents' participation in programs (e.g., determining eligibility) they should consider parents' efforts (or intentions) to obtain education and skills training; engage in activities designed to maximize family self-sufficiency (e.g., job search, work); look to parents’ efforts to secure needed medical care for their children; and assess cooperation with program caseworkers. Moreover, states need to ensure that family planning is voluntary and accessible – but never linked as a condition of obtaining or retaining benefits – for those persons who want to space births or limit the number of their children. (ACF [Administration for Children and Families], 1999). In other words, states can help parents on welfare become self-sufficient by evaluating their efforts to prepare for, obtain, and participate in job search and other family self-sufficiency activities, rather than judging the size of their families. Moreover, family planning should be voluntary and accessible so that all eligible applicants who want it can obtain it. To perform this technique, you hold your index and middle finger over your fourth string (the 'low' E string) on your instrument, your ring finger over the second string (high E), your little (or pinky) finger covers your second highest string (B), your middle finger covers the A string, and your thumb covers the bass (high E) string. You should make sure each finger is lightly touching the string without making a firm pluck, then when you all press down together they mute the individual strings so only one is picking out a note from each chord. It takes a bit of practice to get your finger combinations comfortable, but five finger fillet makes it easy to quickly learn simple melodies on the guitar. prompt: Why are sexist jokes funny?
response:
Many people believe that sexual humor plays a valuable social role and can provide entertainment without being inherently degrading or demeaning to those involved, either explicitly (when people are the explicit objects of a joke) or implicitly (when a group identity they are identified with is the butt of a joke). These so-called 'playful' sexual jokes typically feature two conditions which would render them unlikely to have a positive humorous effect. These conditions are known as 'benign' transgression and inequity effects. Benign transgression occurs when those subjected to the verbal harassment may derive some pleasure from the experience (e.g. laughing) thereby validating them (e.g. they feel accepted/included/part of ‘in on the joke’) and those delivering the verbal harassment derive amusement (e.g. making laughter is cathartic). In contrast, verbal harassment should rightly not make those subjected to the verbal harassment ‘feel validated’/’in on the joke’ and rightly cause amusement of those being offended. Thus 'playful' sexual harassment cannot involve verbal taunting/belittling the persons being offended.

Inquity effects explain why 'playful' sexual comments can be offensive even when they are not verbal taunting/belittling. These effects occur when those subjected to the verbal harassment benefit from higher status persons displaying knowledge, affection, or admiration thereby denying the lower status persons the higher status associated with having knowledge, admiration, or higher admiration. 'Playful' sexual comments deny females higher status associated with intelligence, emotional intelligence, and respect. 'Playful' sexual comments deny males higher status associated with honor, competence, and respect. 'Playful' comments can be verbal teasing or put-downs if higher status persons deny lower status persons higher status associated with honor, competence, and respect when they mock lower status persons. 'Playful' comments mock persons by denying them higher status associated with intelligence, emotional intelligence, and respect. 'Playful' comments belittle persons by mocking them.
